questions.question: Who among the following was a great advocate of English education in India?
questions.solution:
T.B. Macaulay is famous for his 'Minute on Education' (1835), which advocated for English-medium education in India.
  • He wanted to create a class of 'Indians in blood and color, but English in taste'.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of British India from 1773 to 1785?
questions.solution:
Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773–1785).
  • He abolished the Dual System of Government.

questions.question: hich city was the capital of the French Colony in India?
questions.solution:
Pondicherry (now Puducherry) was the capital of French India.
  • It remained under French control until 1954.

questions.question: Who among the following was a freedom fighter, based on whose design the present Indian National Flag is designed?
questions.solution:
Pingali Venkaiah designed the basic structure of the Indian National Flag.
  • The current design was officially adopted on 22 July 1947.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact was signed in ______.
questions.solution:
The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 between the INC and the Muslim League.
  • It also saw the reunion of the Moderates and Extremists.

questions.question: n which year was Sri Lanka discovered by the Portuguese?
questions.solution:
The Portuguese explorer Lourenço de Almeida reached Sri Lanka in 1505.
  • They controlled the coastal areas for spice trade for over 150 years.

questions.question: In which year did the British Government announce Morley-Minto Reforms in India?
questions.solution:
The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
  • This is often seen as the seeds of communalism in Indian politics.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Congress Party led by Indira Gandhi give the slogan of ‘Garibi Hatao’ (‘Remove poverty’) in the Lok Sabha elections?
questions.solution:
Indira Gandhi used the slogan 'Garibi Hatao' during the 1971 Lok Sabha elections.
  • It helped her win a landslide victory.

questions.question: hich Committee among the following was formed in Bombay in March 1919?
questions.solution:
The Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 by the Ali brothers (Shaukat and Muhammad Ali).
  • It protested against the harsh treatment of the Caliph of Turkey.

questions.question: The Mughals were descendants of:
questions.solution:
The Mughals were descendants of Timur (on the paternal side) and Genghis Khan (on the maternal side).
  • They preferred to be called Timurids.

questions.question: Who among the following was the president of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly.
  • He later became the first President of India.

questions.question: Which metal did the Harappans get from the present day Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The Harappans obtained Copper from the Khetri mines in Rajasthan.
  • They also imported copper from Oman.

questions.question: he Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama landed in ______ in the year 1498.
questions.solution:
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) in 1498.
  • He was welcomed by the local ruler, the Zamorin.

questions.question: The ______ movement was led by Chaudhary Devi Lal in 1987.
questions.solution:
Chaudhary Devi Lal led the Nyaya Yudh (War for Justice) movement in Haryana in 1987.
  • He later served as the Deputy Prime Minister of India.

questions.question: In 1818, the Holkar Dynasty signed the Treaty of Mandsaur with the ______.
questions.solution:
The Holkar Dynasty (Malhar Rao Holkar) signed the Treaty of Mandsaur with the British in 1818.
  • This followed their defeat in the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the 'Servants of India Society'?
questions.solution:
Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
  • He was considered the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: ho among the following was a saint from Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
Chokhamela was a 14th-century Varkari saint from Maharashtra.
  • He belonged to the Mahar caste and was one of the first Dalit poets in India.

questions.question: he Khalji Dynasty ruled over Delhi from ______.
questions.solution:
The Khalji Dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320.
  • Alauddin Khalji was the most powerful ruler of this dynasty.

questions.question: hola inscriptions describe Tirunamattukkani as '______'.
questions.solution:
In Chola inscriptions, Tirunamattukkani refers to land gifted to temples.
  • Brahmadeya was land gifted to Brahmanas, and Shalabhoga was for school maintenance.

questions.question: As per Section 2 of the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972, ‘Antiquities’ include 'any manuscript, record or other document which is of scientific, historical, literary or aesthetic value and which has been in existence for not less than ______ years'.
questions.solution:
According to the 1972 Act, any manuscript or record must be at least 75 years old to be classified as an Antiquity.
  • For other objects (sculptures, etc.), the limit is usually 100 years.

questions.question: 'Nagara' temples typically have a ______ style of architecture.
questions.solution:
The Nagara style is the North Indian style of temple architecture.
  • The Dravida style is prevalent in South India.

questions.question: othal, a prominent city of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Lothal is located in Gujarat near the Sabarmathi River.
  • It was the world's earliest man-made dockyard.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the Brahmo Covenant, which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj and made a list of the duties and obligations of its members?
questions.solution:
Debendranath Tagore (father of Rabindranath) wrote the Brahmo Covenant.
  • He was the leader of the Tattvabodhini Sabha before joining the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts ended the monopoly of the East India Company over trade with India?
questions.solution:
The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's monopoly over trade with India (except for trade in tea and trade with China).
  • It also allowed Christian missionaries to come to India.

questions.question: In which year was the Home Rule Movement started?
questions.solution:
The Home Rule Movement was started in 1916 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant.
  • It aimed at achieving self-government for India within the British Empire.
